newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Some Turk Cypriots threaten to take over town.
newsitem.headline: Some Turk Cypriots threaten to take over town.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot ultra-nationalist leader Mehmet Arslan at the weekend called on followers to enter the empty Greek Cypriot town of Varosha and lay claim to houses there.
He told a rally late on Saturday at the fence surrounding the abandoned town that a march would be held on March 2, finishing in a mass entry of Varosha.
"We do not believe any of the authorities will stop us...Anyone who likes any of the houses there should spray their name on it, that house will then be theirs," Arslan said.
"I wholeheartedly support this march," said Kenan Akin, the Turkish Cypriot "minister of agriculture and forests" who attended the meeting.

The island has been divided since 1974 when Turkish forces invaded after Greek Cypriots staged a coup backed by the military regime then ruling Greece. Negotiations to unite the two communities in a federation have stalled.
Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktas said two weeks ago that people would not be settled in Varosha unless Greek Cypriots went ahead with plans to buy anti-aircraft missiles from Russia.
Denktas heads a Turkish Cypriot breakaway state in the northern third of the island. Only Ankara recognises the breakaway state and has some 30,000 troops stationed there.

Varosha, called Maras in Turkish, was a seaside resort town before the 1974 invasion, when the Greek Cypriot population fled south. The Turkish Cypriot administration has kept the town empty since then.

Turkish Cypriot police said on Sunday that they had arrested Savaa Sidereno, aged 22, a Greek Cypriot who crossed on Saturday night the "green line" that divides the two communities near the village of Athna close to a British military base.
A Greek Cypriot couple, who were reported to have sought asylum in northern Cyprus, returned home to the south on Friday saying they got lost.
Tension between the two communities has risen since the Cyprus government announced plans to buy the Russian missiles, due to be deployed in about 16 months.
